title: July 2026 Mining Forecast
body: At ADW the fleet plan can show 83% availability on a machine that's still delivering next to nothing in BCM, because "available" and "producing" are two different numbers. If you only check the top-line avail% in the morning report, you'll miss units that are mechanically fine but parked on swing or rehandle duty — and that gap is exactly where production shortfalls hide until month-end.
keyPoints: Availability and utilization are not the same metric — EX-263 sat at 83.1% planned availability but only 4.2% utilization in one fortnight because it was deliberately parked on swing cover. A fully available machine contributing almost nothing is a planning decision, not a breakdown, and it needs to show up in your head count the same way a down machine does.

A unit with "no recovery window" in the plan (like EX-104, offline the entire month on pump failure) quietly removes a full excavator's capacity from every daily target until someone forces a repair date onto the schedule.

Stacking two major services in the same week — even on your most reliable unit — compresses production without a single breakdown occurring. Check the service calendar for collisions before you commit to a daily number.
Forecasts are built on textbook conditions and explicitly exclude breakdowns, weather, and comms issues — treat the forecast BCM as a ceiling, not a commitment, once reality intervenes.
apply: When you scan this morning's availability sheet, don't stop at the avail% column — cross-check which machines are flagged swing or rehandle, because that's where a "healthy" fleet count can still leave you short at the loading face.
